## tts/client

Speech, asked of a connection in the OpenAI shape: `POST
audio/speech` with a model, a voice and a speed, a WAV clip back. Kokoro-FastAPI
and OpenAI answer in WAV; OpenRouter has none, and is asked for MP3, which is
decoded (`tts/decode.js`). Kokoro also lists its voices at `audio/voices`; a
server with no such thing lists none, which is not an error.

## SpeechConnection

Where a request goes, and how: a connection and a model, as
`speechConnectionOf` makes them.

Type: [Object][184]

### Properties

- `endpoint` **[string][185]** The API's base, e.g. `http://localhost:8880/v1`
- `apiKey` **[string][185]?** Sent as a bearer token when present
- `model` **[string][185]** `kokoro`, `tts-1`, `hexgrad/kokoro-82m`
- `type` **[string][185]?** The connection's type: OpenRouter's is asked
  for MP3, and for its routing
- `routing` **Record<[string][185], any>?** OpenRouter's `provider` field, as
  a chat on the connection sends it
- `inputLimit` **[number][186]?** The most one request may say, in
  characters; a longer text is asked for in pieces

## SpeechRequest

What to say, and how.

Type: [Object][184]

### Properties

- `input` **[string][185]**&#x20;
- `voice` **[string][185]** Passed through as written: a name, or a Kokoro mix
- `speed` **[number][186]?** 1 when absent

## tts/cut

A paragraph too long for one request, cut into pieces that
fit. OpenAI reads at most 4096 characters at a time, and so do some of
OpenRouter's models. Each piece is whole sentences where a sentence fits,
so the voice ends each piece where a reader would pause anyway; a sentence
longer than the limit is cut between words, and a word longer than that
where it reaches it.

## tts/decode

Compressed audio made a WAV clip, for a server that gives no
WAV: OpenRouter answers in MP3 or in raw samples at a rate it doesn't say.
The browser decodes it, at the rate Kokoro and OpenAI speak at, and the clip
then joins any other (`tts/wav.js`). The one place in `tts/` that needs an
audio context.

## SAMPLE_RATE

Samples a second: what Kokoro and OpenAI answer in, so their clips and these join.

## tts

A document read aloud by a speech server, in the project's
voices. Pure: nothing here holds state or touches a store. The
`useNarration` composable does, and this is what it is made of.

- **script** - A document as blocks to be spoken, a paragraph each, and who
  speaks each: an overlay that survives edits
- **reading** - What the server is asked for: each block in its voice, known
  by a signature its audio is kept under
- **hints** - Pronunciation hints, `word:say`, applied to what is sent
- **filters** - Regular expressions for what is not read: page numbers, reference marks
- **voices** - The project's voices, their colours, and the default
- **highlight** - Where each speaker's lines are in a document, to colour, and what is skipped
- **client** - Speech asked of a connection in the OpenAI shape, a WAV clip back
- **cut** - A paragraph too long for one request, cut at sentence ends
- **decode** - Compressed audio made a WAV clip, for OpenRouter, which gives no WAV
- **wav** - Clips joined into one track, and where in it each plays
- **player** - Audio handed to the page: an object URL, or a clip played to its end

Design: `.llm/narration_design.md`.

### Examples

```javascript
import { blocksOf, resolveSpeakers } from '@/tts/script.js'
const blocks = blocksOf(document.content)
const speakers = resolveSpeakers(
  blocks.map(b => b.text),
  document.speakers
)
```

## tts/player

WAV audio, handed to the page to play: as an object URL for a
player of the page's own, or played here through to its end.

## tts/reading

What a reading asks the speech server for, and what it has.

Each block is one utterance: its words after the filters and the hints,
in its speaker's voice. An utterance is known by its signature — the
connection and model it is asked of, the voice as the server is asked for
it, the speed, and the words — and audio is kept by signature. So whatever
changes what would be said — an edit, a new speaker, a voice remixed, a
hint, a filter, another model — leaves that block without audio and every
other with the audio it had. Putting the words back brings it back. A block
the filters take all of is skipped: nothing is asked for.

## BLOCK_GAP

Type: [number][186]

## tts/script

A document as something to be read aloud: its blocks, and
who speaks each.

A block is a paragraph: any node that holds text, with the markdown taken
off. It is the smallest thing that can have a speaker of its own, and one
request to the speech server. Speech is not stood apart from the narration
around it within a paragraph. That was tried, so that a character could
have the line and the narrator the tag, and it reads badly: a sentence cut
at its quotation marks is said as two or three, each ending where it was
cut, with a pause in the middle of it. A character's line is given a voice
by giving them the paragraph.

The document is the writer's, and nothing here is written into it. The
speakers are an overlay. Each assignment remembers the block it was made
on — its text, and where it was — and is found again by the text, at the
nearest place to where it was, when the document has changed since. A
block that has moved keeps its speaker; two that read the same keep theirs
apart; one that has been rewritten finds nothing, and reads in the default
voice again. Nobody can say who speaks a line that no longer exists.

## spoken

### Parameters

- `node` &#x20;

## spoken

One node's text as it should be spoken: its words with the marks taken
off, and a line break where the writer ended a line. One character to a
document position, so an offset into it is an offset into the node.

### Parameters

- `node` &#x20;

Returns **[string][185]**&#x20;

Type: [Object][184]

## blocksOfDoc

A document's blocks, in reading order, as they are to be spoken.

Every node that holds text is one — a paragraph proper, a heading, a list
item, a quoted line — with the markdown taken off. Code is not read aloud,
nor a table, which is a grid to look along rather than something said; and
a rule has nothing to say. Nothing empty is kept.

### Parameters

- `doc` &#x20;

Returns **[Array][192]<[Block][123]>**&#x20;

## assignSpeaker

The assignments to keep after some blocks are given a speaker, or given
back to the default voice. Written from the blocks as they stand, so an
assignment whose block is gone goes with it rather than piling up.

### Parameters

- `texts` **[Array][192]<[string][185]>** The blocks' texts
- `speakers` **[Array][192]<([string][185] | null)>** As resolved for these blocks
- `indices` **[Array][192]<[number][186]>** The blocks changing hands
- `voiceId` **([string][185] | null)** Their speaker, or null for the default voice

Returns **[Array][192]\<SpeakerAssignment>**&#x20;

## kept

Type: [Array][192]\<SpeakerAssignment>

## tts/voices

A project's voices: who reads it, and who speaks in it.

A voice is a name for the writer, what the server is asked for, and a
colour to know its lines by. A project with none has one, a narrator,
until the writer makes the list their own; the first change writes the
whole list, that one and all. One voice is the default, and reads whatever
nobody else has been given.

## DEFAULT_VOICES

## DEFAULT_VOICES

## DEFAULT_VOICES

The voice a project starts with: a Kokoro mix that reads fiction well.
`af_nicole` carries it and is slow on its own, so the others and the speed
bring it up to a reading pace.

## VOICE_COLORS

The colours a voice can have, for telling speakers apart at a glance.
Shown behind text at a fraction of their strength, so they read on a light
page and a dark one.

## nextColor

A colour for a new voice: the first nobody has, and once they all have
one, the next around.

### Parameters

- `voices` **[Array][192]\<TtsVoice>**&#x20;

Returns **[string][185]**&#x20;

## SAMPLE_TEXT

What a voice says when the writer wants to hear it.

Type: [string][185]

## voicesOf

The project's voices: its own, or the default while it has none.

### Parameters

- `narration` **(StoryNarration | null | [undefined][193])**&#x20;

Returns **[Array][192]\<TtsVoice>**&#x20;

## defaultVoiceOf

The default voice, which reads whatever nobody else has been given: the
one chosen, while it is still there, else the first. A project that chose
one while the choice was called the narrator still has it.

### Parameters

- `narration` **(StoryNarration | null | [undefined][193])**&#x20;
- `voices` **[Array][192]\<TtsVoice>?** As `voicesOf` gives them (optional, default `voicesOf(narration)`)

Returns **[string][185]** A voice id

##

Type: [string][185]

## voiceFor

The voice a block is read in: its speaker, while that voice is still
there, else the default.

### Parameters

- `voices` **[Array][192]\<TtsVoice>**&#x20;
- `voiceId` **([string][185] | null | [undefined][193])** The block's speaker, if any
- `defaultVoiceId` **[string][185]**&#x20;

Returns **TtsVoice**&#x20;

## tts/wav

WAV files, read and written by hand: enough to join the clips
a speech server returns into one track, a breath between paragraphs, and
to know where in the track each clip starts. Byte-level, so it needs no
audio context and runs the same under test as on the page.

## WavFormat

Type: [Object][184]

### Properties

- `channels` **[number][186]**&#x20;
- `sampleRate` **[number][186]**&#x20;
- `bitsPerSample` **[number][186]**&#x20;

## tag

### Parameters

- `view` &#x20;
- `at` &#x20;

## tag

Four ASCII bytes as the chunk id they spell.

### Parameters

- `view` **[DataView][196]**&#x20;
- `at` **[number][186]**&#x20;

## Track

A track: the clips as one file, and where in it each plays.

The file is given in parts — a header, then each clip's samples and the
silences between as they already stand in memory — for a `Blob` to be
made of. A chapter is tens of megabytes, and joining it into one buffer
first would hold it all twice.

Type: [Object][184]

### Properties

- `parts` **[Array][192]<[Uint8Array][197]>** One WAV file, in order
- `segments` **[Array][192]<{start: [number][186], end: [number][186]}>** Each clip's place in the track, in seconds
- `duration` **[number][186]** The whole track, in seconds

## parseWav

Read a WAV file.

The data chunk's declared length is not trusted. A server that streams
its answer writes the header before it knows how long the answer is, and
leaves the length at zero or at the most it could be; the data then runs
to the end of the file.

### Parameters

- `buffer` **[ArrayBuffer][190]**&#x20;

<!---->

- Throws **[Error][191]** When it is not a WAV file, or has no data

Returns **Wav**&#x20;

## format

Type: ([WavFormat][155] | null)

## bytesPerSecond

### Parameters

- `format` **[WavFormat][155]**&#x20;

Returns **[number][186]** Bytes per second of audio

## durationOf

How long a clip plays.

### Parameters

- `wav` **Wav**&#x20;

Returns **[number][186]** Seconds

## wavHeader

The 44 bytes that open a PCM WAV file holding so much data.

### Parameters

- `format` **[WavFormat][155]**&#x20;
- `dataLength` **[number][186]** Bytes of samples to follow

Returns **[Uint8Array][197]**&#x20;

## write

### Parameters

- `at` **[number][186]** @param {string} text
- `text` &#x20;

## concatParts

Parts as one buffer.

### Parameters

- `parts` **[Array][192]<[Uint8Array][197]>**&#x20;

Returns **[ArrayBuffer][190]**&#x20;

## encodeWav

Write a WAV file: a header, then the parts as given, PCM.

### Parameters

- `format` **[WavFormat][155]**&#x20;
- `parts` **[Array][192]<[Uint8Array][197]>**&#x20;

Returns **[ArrayBuffer][190]**&#x20;

## joinClips

The clips as one track, a pause between each, and where in it each plays.

Every clip must be in the format of the first. A speech server answers in
one format, and joining two would mean decoding, which this does not do.
The pause is silence for 16-bit and wider PCM, which is what a server
sends; 8-bit WAV puts silence at 128, and would get a faint click.

### Parameters

- `clips` **[Array][192]<[ArrayBuffer][190]>**&#x20;
- `$1` **[Object][184]** (optional, default `{}`)
  - `$1.gap` (optional, default `0.4`)

<!---->

- Throws **[Error][191]** With no clips, or clips that differ in format

Returns **[Track][161]**&#x20;

## data

Type: [Array][192]<[Uint8Array][197]>

## segments

Type: [Array][192]<{start: [number][186], end: [number][186]}>

## segmentAt

Which segment is playing at a moment: the one it falls in, or the one
about to start during the pause before it.

### Parameters

- `track` **{segments: [Array][192]<{start: [number][186], end: [number][186]}>}**&#x20;
- `time` **[number][186]** Seconds into the track

Returns **([number][186] | null)** A segment index, or null past the end
